topicName: Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, and Hybrid Scenarios
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, and Hybrid Scenarios in Microsoft SQL Server"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a comprehensive guide to understanding and deploying Microsoft SQL Server workloads across Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and Hybrid scenarios. Choosing the right deployment option is critical for optimizing performance, cost, and compatibility."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Azure SQL Deployment Options"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure provides three primary deployment models for SQL Server workloads. Azure SQL Database is a fully managed Platform as a Service (PaaS) database engine best suited for modern cloud applications. Azure SQL Managed Instance offers near 100% compatibility with the SQL Server engine on-premises, making it ideal for lift-and-shift migrations. Finally, SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines provides IaaS capabilities for complete OS and database-level control."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Deploying an Azure SQL Database using T-SQL"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can provision an Azure SQL Database dynamically using Azure CLI or T-SQL scripts connected to your logical server. Below is an example of creating a database with specific service objectives."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"CREATE DATABASE SalesDB (EDITION = 'GeneralPurpose', SERVICE_OBJECTIVE = 'GP_Gen5_2', MAXSIZE = 50 GB);"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Implementing Hybrid Scenarios with Azure Arc"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Hybrid scenarios allow organizations to bridge on-premises SQL Server instances with Azure services using Azure Arc. Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server extends Azure management and security to instances hosted outside of Azure, including on-premises datacenters and multi-cloud environments."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Centralized Inventory: View all your SQL Server instances across on-premises and cloud in the Azure Portal."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Advanced Security: Leverage Microsoft Defender for Cloud to detect threats and vulnerabilities on non-Azure SQL servers."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Best Practices Assessment: Run automated configuration assessments to ensure high availability and performance optimization."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Configuring Distributed Availability Groups for Hybrid DR"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"For hybrid disaster recovery (DR) solutions between an on-premises SQL Server instance and an Azure SQL Managed Instance, you can configure a Distributed Availability Group. This architecture links two separate availability groups without requiring them to reside in the same domain or network topology."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"CREATE AVAILABILITY GROUP [HybridAG]
WITH (DISTRIBUTED)
AVAILABILITY GROUP ON
  'OnPremAG' WITH (
    LISTENER_URL = 'tcp://onprem-listener.domain.com:5022',
    AVAILABILITY_MODE = SYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT
  ),
  'AzureMIAG' WITH (
    LISTENER_URL = 'tcp://azuredb-listener.public.database.windows.net:5022',
    AVAILABILITY_MODE = ASYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT
  );"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"By leveraging Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, and hybrid features like Azure Arc and Distributed Availability Groups, database administrators can design resilient, scalable, and secure data estates that span both on-premises infrastructure and the Microsoft Azure cloud."}]
